title: Round 6 B3: boulders at a believable size
question: Do these read as boulders (rock at player scale) rather than the two-cell pimples the old dome-halving bug produced? Too spiky/thin for a 'boulder', or is that fine given B2's residuals cover the squatter end already?
context_md:
canyon seed 6, world 2048x640, 2 boulder markers both seated. Taller one (right) measures 6 cells tall (viewshot's own print caps at 6; the uncapped test measures p50 12 / max 30 across canyon seeds 1..=600) and stands 14 cells proud of its flanks -- even with the player.

Fixed: width 2-5 -> 3-13, height was `height.min(width)` (1x) now drawn independently up to the design's real 3x-width ceiling, and the dome's *visible* semi-axis is used directly instead of implicitly halved (round 4's bug: a drawn '4 tall' boulder only rose 2 rows above ground).

Also found and fixed along the way (affects both boulders and B2's residuals): a seated feature that only converts its single top soil cell can end up structurally floating -- present, attached, reading solid, but with zero path to any anchor -- if its whole footprint sits over a soil blanket deep enough that no edge reaches bare rock. Caught by the pre-existing `every_solid_is_anchored` test, not by anything this track built new.
